question: Which of the following is NOT a complete protein source?
solution:
The correct answer is **Nuts.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Protein Source:**

__
 
• A protein is made up of **20 distinct kinds of amino acids**, which are ch**emical substances bonded to one another**. **11 different kinds of amino acids are naturally produced by our bodies.**
 
• However, humans must obtain the remaining **nine varieties of amino acids, known as "essential amino acids," from other sources**, such the food we consume.
 
• The nine essential amino acids are **valine, tryptophan, phenylalanine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, and phenylalanine.**

**Incomplete Protein:**

 
• An **"incomplete protein"** is defined as protein that **does not include all nine types of amino acids** that must be obtained from diet.
 
• Examples of incomplete proteins include:
 
 
• **Seeds and Nuts**
 
• Complete grains (like brown rice or whole-wheat bread)
 
• ‌Vegetables
 
• legumes, such as beans, peas, and lentils.
 
 

**Complete Protein:**

 
• A protein is referred described as being "complete" if it contains all nine different types of amino acids that you must obtain from diet.
 
• Animal sources provide a complete source of protein (i.e. containing all essential amino acids), whereas vegetable sources generally lack one or more of the essential amino acids.
 
• Great sources of complete proteins are:
 
 
• **‌Fish**
 
• **‌Poultry (chicken, duck, or turkey)**
 
• **‌Eggs**
 
• **‌Dairy products (milk, yogurt, or cheese, for example)**
 
• **‌Beef or pork**
 
• **‌Soy products, such as tofu and edamame **
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Proteins:**

 
• Proteins are the **building blocks of life**. Every cell in the human body contains protein. The basic structure of a protein is a chain of amino acids.
 
• Protein foods are broken down into parts **called amino acids during digestion**. The **human body needs a number of amino acids in large enough amounts to maintain good health.**
 
• Amino acids are **found in animal sources such as meats, milk, fish, and eggs**.
 
• They are** also found in plant sources such as soy, beans, legumes, nut kinds of butter, and some grains (such as wheat germ and quinoa).**
 
• You do not need to eat animal products to get all the protein you need in your diet.
 
• The rich sources of proteins are egg, milk, yoghurt, fish and seafood, soya, pistachio nuts, pork, chicken.
 
• They are also found in plant sources such as soy, beans, legumes, nut kinds of butter, and some grains (such as wheat germ and quinoa).
 
• Amino acids are classified into three groups:
 
 
• **Essential **
 
• **Nonessential **
 
• **Conditional**
 
 
 
• **Essential amino acids** cannot be made by the body and must be supplied by food.
 
 
• They do not need to be eaten at one meal.
 
• The balance over the whole day is more important.
 
 
 
• **Nonessential amino acids** are made by the body from essential amino acids or in the normal breakdown of proteins.
 
• **Conditional amino acids** are needed in times of illness and stress.
